source.title: Your intellectual fly is open when you use an LLM to author a post (2025)
source.author: cyb0rg0

title.zh: LLM生成内容为何暴露写作者声音
title.en: Why LLM-Generated Content Exposes Its Author

excerpt.zh: LLM生成内容正在社交平台留下明显的文风痕迹；真正的风险不只是尴尬，还包括读者对作者真实性和观点归属的怀疑。
excerpt.en: LLM-generated content often leaves recognizable stylistic traces online, risking not just embarrassment but also readers’ trust in an author’s authenticity.

disclosure.zh: 本文使用星期天AI中转站大模型，基于 Hacker News 内容自动生成。
disclosure.en: This article was automatically generated by the Weekly Day AI gateway model using content from Hacker News.

text.zh: LLM生成内容与个人声音
text.en: LLM-Generated Content and Personal Voice

text.zh: LLM生成内容已经成为职业社交平台上的常见现象。文章作者认为，问题不在于人们使用工具，而在于让模型代替自己完成表达，结果常常产生一种读者能够迅速辨认的、不像本人的文风。
text.en: LLM-generated content has become a visible presence on professional social platforms. The author’s objection is not to using the tools themselves, but to letting a model replace the writer’s expression, often producing a style that readers can quickly recognize as unlike the person posting it.

text.zh: 这篇文章以LinkedIn为主要场景展开。作者说，平台主动提供“用AI改写”等功能，降低了使用门槛；但在他的观察中，许多由模型生成或重写的帖子并不只是平庸，而是带有重复、刺耳的格式和措辞。
text.en: The article focuses on LinkedIn. The author notes that platform features such as AI rewriting make these tools easy to use, but argues that many generated or rewritten posts are not merely mediocre. They carry repetitive, distracting patterns in both formatting and wording.

text.zh: 读者识别到的文风信号
text.en: The Stylistic Signals Readers Notice

text.zh: 作者列举了若干他认为反复出现的信号，包括大量表情符号、单句段落、固定的对比句式，以及不符合作者自然习惯的破折号。单个特征并不能证明文本由AI完成，但多个模式同时出现，会让读者产生强烈的机器生成感。
text.en: The author points to recurring signals such as abundant emojis, one-sentence paragraphs, familiar contrastive constructions, and em dashes used in ways that do not match the writer’s usual habits. None of these features proves that AI wrote a passage, but several appearing together can create a strong impression of machine-generated prose.

text.zh: 这种判断的影响超出了审美层面。当读者明显感觉一篇帖子不是作者亲自写的，就可能进一步怀疑其中的经历、判断和观点究竟有多少是真实表达。文章的结论很直接：无法确认内容是否属于作者本人时，读者可能干脆停止阅读。
text.en: The effect goes beyond matters of taste. When readers sense that a post was not written by its apparent author, they may also question how much of its experience, judgment, and opinion is genuine. The article’s conclusion is blunt: when authorship becomes uncertain, readers may simply stop reading.

text.zh: LLM更适合辅助而非代写
text.en: LLMs Work Better as Assistants Than Ghostwriters

text.zh: 作者并不否定大语言模型的价值。他认为，模型适合头脑风暴、帮助理解文本，也可以充当高效编辑。这个区分提供了更稳妥的使用框架：让工具帮助整理和检验已有想法，而不是把尚未形成的观点包装成看似完整的成文内容。
text.en: The author does not reject the value of large language models. He considers them useful for brainstorming, understanding text, and serving as effective editors. This distinction suggests a more cautious workflow: use the tool to organize and test ideas that already exist, rather than wrapping an undeveloped viewpoint in polished-looking prose.

text.zh: 真实性风险仍待观察
text.en: The Remaining Question of Authenticity

text.zh: 文章的判断来自个人观察和强烈的文风批评，并没有提供检测准确率或读者调查，因此不能把这些特征当成可靠的AI鉴定标准。不同平台、语言和写作习惯也可能改变读者的判断。更合理的启示是关注文本是否具体、可信、符合作者一贯声音，而不是寻找一套固定的“AI标记”。
text.en: The argument is based on personal observation and a forceful critique of style; it provides no detection accuracy figures or reader survey. These signals therefore should not be treated as a reliable AI-authorship test. Platform norms, languages, and individual writing habits can all affect perception. A more useful lesson is to ask whether a post is specific, credible, and consistent with its author’s established voice, rather than searching for a fixed set of AI markers.

text.zh: 把表达的功劳留给作者
text.en: Keep the Credit for Expression

text.zh: 这场争论最终指向一个简单的编辑原则：工具可以改进表达，但不应掩盖表达者。对需要建立信任的职业内容而言，保留个人语气、具体经验和真实判断，可能比追求一篇无瑕却千篇一律的帖子更重要。作者因此呼吁，人们对自己的声音保持信心，亲自写下真正想说的话。
text.en: The debate ultimately points to a simple editorial principle: tools may improve expression, but they should not obscure the person expressing it. For professional content that depends on trust, preserving an individual tone, concrete experience, and genuine judgment may matter more than producing a flawless but interchangeable post. The author’s recommendation is to trust one’s own voice and write what one actually means.
